examples.ko: 상자 겉면에 주소를 크게 적어 주세요.
examples.en: Please write the address in large letters on the outside of the box.

examples.ko: 이 과일은 겉면이 매끈하고 윤기가 나요.
examples.en: The surface of this fruit is smooth and shiny.

examples.ko: 겉면만 보고 속을 판단하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't judge the inside just by the outside.
The outside of the frying pan is very hot, so be careful.
The expiration date is printed on the outside of the package.
Please bake the outside of the bread until it's golden brown.

explain: '겉'보다 좀 더 구체적으로, 상자·과일·책처럼 면이 있는 물건의 바깥쪽 면을 말할 때 자연스러워요. 반대말은 '속'이나 '안쪽'이에요. 사람의 성격처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에는 '겉면'보다 '겉'을 써요.
explain_en: It is a little more specific than '겉': it fits the outer face of things that have a surface, such as boxes, fruit and books. Its opposites are '속' and '안쪽'. For things you cannot see, like a person's character, use '겉' rather than '겉면'.

examples.en: I sort the trash by type.
Could you tell the twins apart from the start?
I'm going to separate the items by color.
It's hard to tell the two words apart.

examples.ko: 일하는 시간과 쉬는 시간을 구분해서 지내요.
examples.en: I keep work time and rest time separate.
Please tell me slowly how to distinguish them.

explain: '구분하다'는 기준을 두고 나눌 때 써요. '구별하다'는 차이를 알아본다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 'A와 B를 구분하다', '~으로 구분하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 구분하다 is used when you divide things by some standard. 구별하다 leans more toward noticing the difference. It appears as 'A와 B를 구분하다' (tell A from B) or '~으로 구분하다' (divide into ~).

examples.en: The bird flapped its wings strongly and took off.
The butterfly's wing flapping looks very light.
The baby bird started clumsy flapping of its wings.
I can hear the buzzing of the bee's wings.
A hummingbird flaps its wings dozens of times a second.

examples.ko: 날갯짓 몇 번에 새는 하늘 높이 올랐어요.
examples.en: With a few flaps of its wings, the bird rose high into the sky.

explain: '날갯짓하다'처럼 동사로도 쓰고, '날개를 퍼덕이다'보다 움직임을 짧게 말하는 느낌이에요. '새로운 날갯짓을 시작하다'처럼 도전의 시작을 비유할 때도 있어요.
explain_en: It can also be used as the verb '날갯짓하다', and it sounds more compact than '날개를 퍼덕이다'. It is sometimes used figuratively, as in '새로운 날갯짓을 시작하다', for starting a new challenge.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 다단계 판매로 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: That company got in trouble over multilevel sales.

examples.ko: 친구가 다단계 사업을 같이 하자고 해서 거절했어요.
examples.en: A friend asked me to join a multilevel business and I refused.
You must be careful about the multilevel method from the start.

examples.ko: 이 로켓은 다단계 구조로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This rocket has a multistage structure.

examples.ko: 다단계 업체에 돈을 맡겼다가 손해를 봤어요.
examples.en: He entrusted money to a multilevel firm and lost out.
They are selling the new product through multilevel distribution.

explain: 여러 단계로 이루어진 구조를 말하지만, 일상에서는 사람을 모아 물건을 파는 '다단계 판매'의 뜻으로 가장 많이 써요. 이때는 조심하라는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 로켓이나 과정처럼 단계가 여럿이라는 뜻으로도 쓰여요.
explain_en: It means a structure of several stages, but in daily life it is most commonly '다단계 판매' (multilevel sales), which carries a cautionary, negative tone. It can also mean multistage things like rockets or processes.

examples.en: In winter, I crave refreshing dongchimi.
I drank a bowl of dongchimi broth.
My mother made dongchimi herself.
I eat noodles with dongchimi broth.

examples.ko: 동치미는 너무 짜지 않게 담가야 맛있어요.
examples.en: Dongchimi tastes good when it isn't made too salty.
This restaurant is famous for its dongchimi cold noodles.

explain: 국물이 많은 물김치의 한 종류로, 겨울에 특히 많이 먹어요. 고구마나 떡과 같이 먹으면 잘 어울려요. '담그다'는 '담가요'처럼 ㅡ가 빠지는 활용이에요.
explain_en: It is a kind of watery kimchi with lots of broth, and people eat it especially in winter. It goes well with sweet potatoes or rice cakes. The verb '담그다' drops its ㅡ in conjugation, as in '담가요'.

examples.en: When a volcano erupts, magma rises to the surface.
Magma is deep underground.
When magma cools and hardens, it becomes rock.
The temperature of magma is over a thousand degrees.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 마그마와 용암의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In science class, I learned the difference between magma and lava.
He is a scholar who studies the magma underground.

explain: 땅속에 있을 때는 '마그마', 땅 위로 흘러나오면 '용암'이라고 해요. 과학 시간이나 화산 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '용암'이 더 익숙하게 들려요.
explain_en: Underground it is '마그마', and once it flows out onto the surface it is called '용암' (lava). It comes up in science class and volcano news. In everyday talk, '용암' may sound more familiar.

examples.en: In spring, I bought tomato seedlings at the market.
I transplanted the seedlings into a pot.

examples.ko: 아버지는 텃밭에 상추 모종을 심고 계세요.
examples.en: My father is planting lettuce seedlings in the vegetable garden.

examples.ko: 모종이 시들지 않게 물을 자주 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You have to water often so the seedlings don't wilt.
I picked out a few seedlings at the flower shop.
The seedlings grew and bore fruit!

explain: '씨앗'은 아직 심기 전의 것이고, '모종'은 씨앗에서 싹이 터서 옮겨 심을 만큼 자란 어린 식물이에요. 보통 '모종을 사다', '모종을 심다'로 말해요. 텃밭이나 베란다 키우기에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: A 씨앗 is a seed before planting, while a 모종 is a young plant that has already sprouted and is ready to be transplanted. People say 모종을 사다 or 모종을 심다. You hear it often in talk about home vegetable gardens.

examples.en: This bowl has a flower pattern.
They put a traditional pattern on the hanbok.

examples.ko: 벽지 문양은 눈에 띄지 않는 걸로 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked a wallpaper pattern that doesn't stand out.
The geometric design on the carpet is pretty.

examples.ko: 건물 벽에 새겨진 문양의 뜻이 궁금해요.
examples.en: I'm curious about the meaning of the design carved on the building wall.
The price changes depending on the fabric pattern.

explain: 문양은 옷, 그릇, 건물에 반복해서 들어가는 장식 모양이에요. '무늬'는 일상에서 더 흔하게 쓰고, 문양은 전통, 문화, 디자인 이야기에서 더 자주 써요. 옷의 줄무늬는 '줄 문양'보다 '줄무늬'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 문양 is the decorative shape repeated on clothes, dishes, or buildings. 무늬 is more common in daily talk, while 문양 appears more in talk about tradition, culture, and design. For stripes on clothes, 줄무늬 is more natural than 줄 문양.

examples.en: The market has all sorts of things.
I've met every kind of person.

examples.ko: 별별 생각이 다 들어서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: All kinds of thoughts came to me, so I couldn't sleep.
All sorts of stories get posted on the internet.

examples.ko: 오늘은 별별 일이 다 생긴 하루였어요.
examples.en: Today was a day when all sorts of things happened.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 별별 음식을 다 팔아요.
examples.en: That shop sells every kind of food.

explain: '별별' 뒤에는 '사람', '일', '생각' 같은 말이 와서 '별별 사람', '별별 일'처럼 써요. 보통 '다'와 함께 '별별 게 다 있다'라고 하면서 놀라거나 어이없어하는 느낌을 담아요.
explain_en: It is followed by a noun like 사람, 일 or 생각, as in '별별 사람', '별별 일'. It often pairs with 다, as in '별별 게 다 있다', carrying a sense of surprise or disbelief.

en: be proportional to; be in proportion to

examples.en: Effort and grades are not always proportional.
The pay is paid in proportion to the hours worked.

examples.ko: 속도가 두 배가 되면 거리도 두 배가 되어 서로 비례해요.
examples.en: If speed doubles, distance doubles too, so they are proportional.
The price will probably be proportional to the size.
I pay a fee in proportion to my usage.
The number of members is set in proportion to the population.

explain: 'A는 B에 비례한다'처럼 '~에/와 비례하다'로 써요. 한쪽이 커지면 다른 쪽도 같이 커지는 관계예요. 한쪽이 커질 때 다른 쪽이 줄어드는 관계는 '반비례하다'라고 해요. 수학, 과학, 경제 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Use it as '~에/와 비례하다' (A is proportional to B): when one grows, the other grows with it. If one grows while the other shrinks, it is '반비례하다'. It comes up often in math, science and economics.

examples.en: The baby looks at me and smiles sweetly.
The clerk greeted me with a bright smile, which made me feel good.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 언제 봐도 생글생글 밝아요.
examples.en: That child always looks cheerful and smiling whenever I see her.
My daughter ran to the front door with a smile.
That smiling face is so cute.

examples.ko: 무슨 좋은 일이 있는지 하루 종일 생글생글 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: She's been smiling all day, as if something good happened.

explain: 소리 없이 눈과 입으로 부드럽게 자꾸 웃는 모습이에요. '웃다', '인사하다'와 자주 같이 쓰고, 한 번 웃는 '생긋'과 달리 계속 웃는 느낌이에요. 비슷한 말로 '방긋방긋'도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes smiling softly and repeatedly with the eyes and mouth, without sound. It goes with '웃다' or '인사하다', and unlike '생긋', which is a single smile, it feels continuous. A similar word is '방긋방긋'.

examples.en: This cup is made of ceramic.
A ceramic knife is light and sharp.
A ceramic plate breaks if you drop it.
We laid ceramic tiles on the bathroom floor.

examples.ko: 세라믹 프라이팬은 음식이 잘 안 달라붙어요.
examples.en: Food doesn't stick much to a ceramic frying pan.
Ceramic products are strong against heat.

explain: 주로 제품 이름 앞에 붙어서 '세라믹 칼', '세라믹 타일'처럼 써요. 흙을 구워 만든 도자기는 '도자기'라는 말을 더 많이 쓰고, 세라믹은 기술이나 소재 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It mostly sits in front of a product name, as in 세라믹 칼 or 세라믹 타일. For traditional fired-clay ware, 도자기 is the usual word, while 세라믹 shows up in talk about technology and materials.

examples.en: I ate cotton candy at the amusement park.

examples.ko: 아이가 솜사탕을 보고 사 달라고 졸랐어요.
examples.en: The child saw the cotton candy and begged me to buy it.
Cotton candy melts quickly in your mouth.
The pink cotton candy looks like a cloud.

examples.ko: 시장 앞에서 아저씨가 솜사탕을 만들고 있어요.
examples.en: A man is making cotton candy in front of the market.
My hands got sticky after eating cotton candy.

explain: '솜'과 '사탕'을 합친 이름이에요. 놀이공원이나 축제에서 먹는 간식이고 '솜사탕을 만들다/먹다'로 말해요. '솜사탕 같은 구름'처럼 폭신하고 달콤한 느낌을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: The name combines '솜' (cotton fluff) and '사탕' (candy). It is a snack from amusement parks and festivals; you say '솜사탕을 만들다/먹다'. It is also used figuratively, as in '솜사탕 같은 구름', for something soft, fluffy and sweet.

examples.en: When May comes, the scent of acacia flowers fills the air.
I picked acacia flowers and tried eating them.

examples.ko: 아카시아 나무 아래에서 벌들이 꿀을 모아요.
examples.en: Bees collect honey beneath the acacia tree.
Acacia honey is clear and sweet.
Acacias have bloomed fully along the road.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 아카시아 잎으로 가위바위보를 했어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I played rock-paper-scissors with acacia leaves.

explain: 한국에서 '아카시아'라고 부르는 나무는 식물 이름으로는 '아까시나무'예요. 하지만 일상에서는 '아카시아'가 훨씬 흔해요. 오월에 흰 꽃이 피고 '아카시아 꿀'로도 유명해요.
explain_en: The tree Koreans call '아카시아' is botanically '아까시나무', but in daily life '아카시아' is far more common. It has white flowers in May and is also famous for '아카시아 꿀' (acacia honey).

examples.en: I sliced the lotus root thin and made it into a braised side dish.
Boiled lotus root is crunchy when you chew it, so it's tasty.
I bought a bundle of lotus root at the market.

examples.ko: 연근 조림은 도시락 반찬으로 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: Braised lotus root is a popular side dish for lunch boxes.

examples.ko: 연근을 자르면 실 같은 것이 길게 늘어나요.
examples.en: When you cut lotus root, thread-like strands stretch out.

examples.ko: 연근 껍질은 칼로 벗기고 식초물에 담가 두세요.
examples.en: Peel the lotus root with a knife and soak it in vinegar water.

explain: 연꽃의 뿌리 부분을 먹는 채소로, 자르면 구멍이 여러 개 보여요. 간장에 졸인 '연근조림'이 반찬으로 가장 흔하고 튀김이나 전으로도 먹어요.
explain_en: It is the edible root part of the lotus, and you can see several holes when you cut it. The most common dish is soy-braised '연근조림' as a side dish, and it is also eaten fried or as jeon.

en: be revealed; show through; be glimpsed

examples.en: You can sense his anxiety from the way he speaks.

examples.ko: 이 그림에는 작가의 따뜻한 마음이 엿보였어요.
examples.en: The artist's warm heart showed through in this painting.
You can catch a glimpse of the room through the gap in the door.
It was a face where sadness showed behind the smile.

examples.ko: 글 곳곳에서 그 사람의 성격이 엿보여서 재미있어요.
examples.en: His personality shows here and there in his writing, which is fun.
He was a child whose talent was visible from early on.

explain: 겉으로 다 드러나지 않고 일부만 슬쩍 보일 때 써요. 마음, 성격, 재능처럼 속에 있는 것에 많이 쓰고, 그냥 눈에 보이는 것은 '보이다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when something is not fully out in the open but a part of it shows slightly. It is often used for inner things like feelings, personality and talent, while things simply visible to the eye are just '보이다'.

examples.en: I have a habit of reading the morning paper every morning.
The morning paper is delivered to the front of the house at dawn.

examples.ko: 아버지는 조간신문에 난 기사를 보여 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father showed me an article in the morning paper.

examples.ko: 요즘은 조간신문 대신 휴대폰으로 뉴스를 봐요.
examples.en: These days I read the news on my phone instead of the morning paper.
The morning paper is lying at the door.
Morning papers and evening papers come out at different times.

explain: 아침에 나오는 신문이에요. 저녁에 나오는 신문은 '석간신문'이라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 요즘은 종이신문 대신 인터넷으로 보는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: It is a newspaper that comes out in the morning. The evening paper is '석간신문', so it is good to learn them as a pair. These days many people read news online instead of on paper.

en: head of an agency; chief; commissioner

examples.en: The agency head visited the site in person today.
The newly arrived head greeted the staff.
The head presented the new plan at the meeting.
Citizens passed their suggestions on to the head.

examples.ko: 그는 오랜 공무원 생활 끝에 청장이 됐어요.
examples.en: After a long career as a civil servant, he became an agency head.
Both the mayor and the agency head attended this event.

explain: '경찰청장', '소방청장'처럼 앞에 기관 이름을 붙여 불러요. '구청장'은 지방 구청의 책임자라서 따로 불러요. 직접 부를 때는 '청장님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The name of the agency goes in front, as in '경찰청장' (police agency head) and '소방청장' (fire agency head). The head of a district office is a '구청장', which is a separate title. When you address them, say '청장님'.

examples.en: The culprit is presumed to be a man.

examples.ko: 사고 원인은 운전자 실수로 추측되고 있어요.
examples.en: The cause of the accident is presumed to be driver error.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 백 년 전에 지어졌다고 추측되어요.
examples.en: This building is thought to have been built a hundred years ago.
The exact time can't be guessed.

examples.ko: 그렇게 추측되는 이유가 몇 가지 있어요.
examples.en: There are a few reasons why it is presumed so.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 삼백 년 전에 그려진 것으로 추측됐어요.
examples.en: This painting is presumed to have been drawn three hundred years ago.

explain: '~로 추측되다', '~것으로 추측되다'처럼 뉴스나 설명하는 글에서 많이 써요. 말할 때는 '~인 것 같아요', '아마 ~일 거예요'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It appears as '~로 추측되다' or '~것으로 추측되다', mostly in news and explanatory writing. In speech, '~인 것 같아요' or '아마 ~일 거예요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: At the zoo I saw a koala hanging from a tree.
Koalas spend most of the day sleeping.

examples.ko: 호주에 가면 코알라를 안아 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go to Australia, you can hold a koala.

examples.ko: 아이가 코알라 인형을 꼭 안고 잤어요.
examples.en: The child slept hugging the koala doll tightly.
The koala is eating eucalyptus leaves.

examples.ko: 새끼 코알라가 엄마 등에 업혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The baby koala was riding on its mother's back.

explain: '캥거루'와 함께 호주의 대표 동물로 말해요. 유칼립투스 잎을 먹고 하루 대부분을 자서 느긋한 동물이라는 이미지가 있어요.
explain_en: It is mentioned together with 캥거루 as a representative Australian animal. It eats eucalyptus leaves and sleeps most of the day, so it has a relaxed image.

examples.en: A scarecrow stands in the middle of the rice field.
The farmer put up a scarecrow to scare away birds.

examples.ko: 아이들이 허수아비 옷을 입고 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The kids put on scarecrow outfits and took photos.

examples.ko: 허수아비 인형이 가을 축제 분위기를 살려요.
examples.en: A scarecrow doll adds to the autumn festival mood.
These days, it has become hard to see scarecrows.

examples.ko: 허수아비처럼 가만히 서 있지만 말고 도와줘요.
examples.en: Don't just stand still like a scarecrow; help me.

explain: '허수아비'는 논밭에서 새를 쫓으려고 세우는 사람 모양 인형이에요. 말로는 '진짜 힘이 없는 사람'을 놀릴 때도 써요. 가을 들판 풍경과 같이 떠올리는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 그 사장님은 이름만 있을 뿐 허수아비 같아요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로만 자리에 있고 실제 힘이나 결정권이 없는 사람을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who holds a position in name only, without real power or authority.

explain_en: A 허수아비 is a human-shaped figure set up in fields to scare away birds. It can also be used for a person who has no real power. Koreans often picture it in an autumn rice field.

examples.en: You found ten thousand won on the street, so what a lucky break.

examples.ko: 중고 가게에서 새 책을 반값에 샀으니 횡재했어요.
examples.en: I bought a new book at half price at a used shop, so I hit the jackpot.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에 택시가 바로 와서 횡재한 기분이었어요.
examples.en: A taxi came right away on a rainy day, and I felt like I'd struck gold.

examples.ko: 공짜 표가 생기다니 이런 횡재가 어디 있어요!
examples.en: Free tickets? What a windfall!

examples.ko: 이 가격에 이 품질이면 완전 횡재예요.
examples.en: At this price and quality, it's a total steal.

examples.ko: 횡재를 바라지 말고 열심히 일하자고 다짐했어요.
examples.en: I resolved not to hope for windfalls and just work hard.

explain: 뜻하지 않게 큰 이익이나 행운을 얻었을 때 써요. '횡재하다', '횡재를 만나다'처럼 쓰고, 구어에서는 '대박'과 비슷하게 말하기도 해요. 값이 싸서 이득을 본 상황에도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you unexpectedly gain a big benefit or stroke of luck. It appears as '횡재하다' and '횡재를 만나다', and in speech it is similar to '대박'. It is also often used when you get a great bargain.
